issues.claim: пока `HttpResponseMessage` не освобождён, соединение занято и не возвращается в пул, поэтому `using` на ответе обязателен
issues.problem: Overstated. With ResponseHeadersRead the connection is released when the content stream is read to the end or when either the stream or the response is disposed, so the response is not the only thing that frees it. The same sentence in en is identical. Disposing the response remains the right advice, but 'required because the connection stays busy until then' is imprecise.
issues.suggestedFix: Say that until the body is read to the end or the response (or its stream) is disposed, the connection stays busy and does not return to the pool, so always dispose the response with `using`. Apply the same change to en.

issues.claim: harness: none for a BCL-only snippet
issues.problem: The snippet needs only the BCL (HttpClient, File). The executable-code rule says BCL-only code is runnable whatever the topic. harness: none is acceptable for a `single` question, but a stub HttpMessageHandler would make the snippet runnable and verifiable.
issues.suggestedFix: Optional. Keep harness: none, or rewrite the snippet as a self-contained program with a fake handler.

issues.claim: продолжал ходить на старый, пока старый кластер не выключили, после чего начал падать с ошибками соединения. Помог только перезапуск.
issues.problem: The scenario is mechanically inconsistent. When the old cluster is shut down, the pooled connection breaks. SocketsHttpHandler then opens a new connection, which resolves DNS again and reaches the new address, so failures would be brief and a restart would not be the only fix. A candidate would learn a wrong failure mode. The en prompt carries the same drift.
issues.suggestedFix: Drop the 'started failing, only restart helped' part. For example: 'All other services switched to the new address within minutes, but this one kept sending requests to the old cluster for days, until the pods were restarted. Metrics on the new cluster show no traffic from it.' Apply the same change to en.

issues.claim: Документация `IHttpClientFactory` прямо советует не использовать типизированные клиенты в singleton-сервисах.
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt of the httpclient-factory page does not show an 'Avoid typed clients in singleton services' section. I recall such a section on that page, but the excerpt does not confirm it. The en explanation repeats the claim.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the claim only if the section is confirmed on the page. Otherwise soften it to: 'typed clients are transient and are not meant to be captured by singletons; the factory docs say HttpClient from the factory is short-lived and must be requested in a timely manner'. That wording is supported by the excerpt.

issues.problem: This holds for a plain SocketsHttpHandler. I cannot confirm from the excerpts whether the default primary handler of AddHttpClient in .NET 10 sets PooledConnectionLifetime from HandlerLifetime. If it does, connections would be recycled and the scenario would not occur. The question also has no meta.dotnetVersion, although the behaviour is version-dependent.
issues.suggestedFix: Verify the default primary handler of Microsoft.Extensions.Http for .NET 10. If the default does not set PooledConnectionLifetime, add meta.dotnetVersion: "10" and say so in the explanation. If it does, redesign the scenario, for example by configuring a primary handler with infinite PooledConnectionLifetime.

issues.problem: Line 7, `builder.Services.AddSingleton<PriceService>();`, is the defect: it gives the transient typed client a singleton lifetime. Line 19 is ordinary constructor injection and is not wrong by itself, because the fix changes the registration and leaves line 19 untouched. Accepting it teaches that normal injection is the bug.
issues.suggestedFix: Use bugLineSets: [[7]] and remove the sentence about line 19 from answer in both locales.
